strings.name: Bruno Mars
strings.summary: Born Peter Gene Hernandez into a Honolulu performing family, Mars moved to Los Angeles and developed as a songwriter and producer before becoming a solo singer. He combines pop, funk, soul and retro showmanship. 24K Magic and Silk Sonic, his partnership with Anderson .Paak, won major Grammys. Collaborations with Mark Ronson, Lady Gaga and ROSÉ widened his audience; he released The Romantic in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His fusion of pop, funk and soul in songwriting and live performance introduces traditional Black musical styles to new audiences.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Performed with his family as a child; moved to Los Angeles after completing high school in 2003.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Retro styles and contemporary pop
strings.highlights.h1.text: Combines funk, soul and pop production across solo releases and collaborations.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Collaborative Grammy achievements
strings.highlights.h2.text: 24K Magic won Album of the Year; Silk Sonic’s Leave the Door Open won Record and Song of the Year among other awards.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Released The Romantic
strings.timeline.t1.text: Returned after a decade without a solo studio album, continuing his exploration of soul and retro pop.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Released cross-genre collaborations
strings.timeline.t2.text: Joined Lady Gaga for Die With a Smile and ROSÉ for APT.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Silk Sonic won major Grammys
strings.timeline.t3.text: Leave the Door Open won Record of the Year, Song of the Year and R&B awards.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Released Silk Sonic album
strings.timeline.t4.text: Collaborated with Anderson .Paak on An Evening with Silk Sonic.
strings.timeline.t5.title: 24K Magic won Album of the Year
strings.timeline.t5.text: The album and its songs received several of that year’s major Grammys.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Released 24K Magic
strings.timeline.t6.text: His third solo album combined funk, R&B and stage-oriented showmanship.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Collaborated on Uptown Funk
strings.timeline.t7.text: Sang and co-wrote Mark Ronson’s international hit.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Released solo debut
strings.timeline.t8.text: Doo-Wops & Hooligans included Just the Way You Are and other early hits.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Moved to Los Angeles
strings.timeline.t9.text: Left Hawaii and gradually entered recording through songwriting and production.
